transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, the main reason I’m here is that I'm really struggling at work. I manage health services, and anything that takes real, sitting-down brain work... it just feels like I hit a wall. 

Like, if I have to do the monthly reports or sit down and plan out a multi-site health event, I just keep putting it off. I know it matters and I know I need to get it done, but I just avoid it. It's starting to become a real problem for me.
Do you feel anxious when you think about doing these tasks?

Not really, no. I wouldn't call it anxiety. I don't get nervous or panicky about the work itself. It's more just... a mental block, I guess. I just can't get myself to start it, but it's not because I'm anxious or worried about it.
Do you have trouble focusing on tasks in your daily life?

Yeah, I definitely do. Um, especially in meetings. I’ll be sitting there, really trying to listen to a budget update, but... it just doesn't take much to pull me away. 

If someone's phone vibrates on the table, or I hear people talking out in the hall, my attention just shifts right to that. Or even just my own thoughts—like, I'll suddenly think about something I forgot to do for the league, and my brain just chases that instead. By the time I tune back in, I realize I've completely missed the last few minutes of what was being said.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I have to be moving all the time or anything like that. I can sit through a long meeting just fine, physically. It's just my mind that wanders off, not my body. I don't really tap my feet or squirm around much.
Do you feel overwhelmed or upset by your inability to focus and complete tasks?

Yeah, it does upset me. I mean... I’m still getting by at work and in the community, for the most part. But it's really frustrating because people have had to cover gaps for me when I drop the ball. Deadlines have slipped on things I'm supposed to be managing. And... well, I’ve definitely embarrassed myself having to make these last-minute apologies to coworkers and friends because I just couldn't pull it together in time. It's not a great feeling, knowing you're letting people down. So, yeah, it does get overwhelming.
Do you often feel guilty or critical of yourself when you're not able to complete tasks or meet expectations?

No, I wouldn't say I really feel guilty. I mean, I don't sit around beating myself up over it or anything. It's frustrating, like I said, and I don't like letting people down, but I don't think I get overly critical of myself. I just try to figure out how to fix whatever I messed up and move on.
Have you always had trouble with focusing and completing tasks, or is this a relatively new development for you?

No, it's not new at all. I've been like this for as long as I can remember. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would tell my parents that I was bright, but I was just always daydreaming. I was constantly losing my worksheets, and I'd forget to turn in my homework unless my mom physically checked my backpack every single night to make sure it was there. So, yeah, it's been an issue my whole life.
Were you more physically active or restless than your peers when you were a child?

No, not really. I wasn't one of those kids bouncing off the walls or anything. Like I was saying, it was more about the daydreaming for me. I was actually a pretty quiet kid, usually just lost in my own head. So, no, I wouldn't say I was more physically active or restless than anyone else.
Do you feel sad or down when you think about your difficulties with focusing and completing tasks?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or down about it. It's just kind of how I am. I mean, it can be annoying when I'm trying to get things done at work and I just can't seem to stay on track, but it doesn't make me depressed or anything. I just try to deal with it as best I can.
Has your difficulty with focusing and completing tasks affected your personal relationships?

Yeah, it definitely has an impact. I mean, I'm still getting by, you know? I haven't lost my job as a clinic manager or anything, and I'm still involved in my community. But... it causes friction. 

People end up having to cover gaps for me because I drop the ball. Deadlines slip by, and I'm constantly having to make these embarrassing, last-minute apologies to my coworkers, or to friends when I forget we had plans or I don't follow through on something I promised. So, it doesn't ruin my relationships completely, but it definitely strains them.
Do you think your difficulties with focusing and completing tasks have caused you significant stress?

Not really. I mean, it's definitely frustrating, like I mentioned with the apologies and scrambling to fix missed deadlines. But I wouldn't call it significant stress. It doesn't keep me up at night or anything like that. It's mostly just... an ongoing annoyance that I've kind of learned to work around over the years.
Do you feel like your difficulties with focusing and completing tasks have caused you a lot of distress?

No, not really. I think it's pretty much like what I just mentioned about the stress. I wouldn't really use the word distress. It's... it's a hassle, you know? I get annoyed with myself when I mess up at the clinic, but it doesn't make me feel deeply overwhelmed or anything like that. I just kind of deal with it as it comes.
Do you feel like your difficulties are affecting your overall happiness?

Not really. I mean... I have a pretty good life. I like my job, and I care about the people around me. The focus issues are just... well, they're frustrating, like I said before. But they don't drag down my mood or make me unhappy in the big picture. I'm doing alright overall, it's really just a hassle I have to manage.
Do you ever feel emotional pain or upset when you think about how your focus issues are impacting your life?

No, I wouldn't say I feel emotional pain over it. It's just like I've been saying... it's a frustration. I don't get deeply upset or sit around feeling bad about it. I just try to fix whatever mistake I made at work and move on. It's really just an annoyance, not something that causes me pain.
